flows.title: Dijkstra on (station, line) states
flows.summary: A node of the search is a pair (station, line). Riding to the next stop costs its minutes, a change of line at the same station costs the transfer time. The number of changes follows from the costs.

steps.note: std::tie gives the ordering needed for std::map.
Priority queue, relaxation, then the path is rebuilt from came_from and grouped into legs.
A small hand-made network where the answer depends on the transfer cost.

flows.title: Fuzzy station search
flows.summary: Exact name, then unique prefix, then substring, then Levenshtein distance. Umlauts and case are normalized first, so “laengenfeldgasse” and “Längenfeldgasse” are the same.

steps.note: Classic dynamic programming with two rows.

flows.title: The network as a graph
flows.summary: Two CSV files describe the U-Bahn: lines with their colours and segments with travel minutes. Stations get integer ids; every segment is added in both directions.

steps.note: Adjacency list: vector of vectors of Connection.

flows.title: Text and HTML output
flows.summary: The same Route is printed for the terminal and exported as a coloured HTML diagram. Station names are escaped before they go into HTML.

flows.title: The terminal program
flows.summary: main.cpp only reads arguments and prints results; all logic is in the library, which is why the same code can run in tests and in this page.

flows.title: C++ in the browser
flows.summary: The library is compiled with Emscripten to WebAssembly. A small Planner class converts C++ results into JavaScript objects; the CSV files are embedded into the module.

steps.note: Search both stations, run Dijkstra, return legs, text and HTML.
One CMake file builds the terminal program, the tests and the WebAssembly module.
